Paleomagnetism and Cyclostratigraphy of the Permian-Triassic
Boundary Interval of the Staroe Slukino Section, Vladimir Region
A. M. Fetisovaa, b, *, R. V. Veselovskiya, b, K. A. Sirotina, b, V. K. Golubevc, and D. V. Rud’kob
a Faculty of Geology, Moscow State University, Moscow, 119991 Russia
b Schmidt Institute of Physics of the Earth, Russian Academy of Sciences, Moscow, 123242 Russia
c Borissiak Paleontological Institute, Russian Academy of Sciences, Moscow, 117647 Russia
*e-mail: anna-fetis@ya.ru
Received August 8, 2022; revised October 29, 2022; accepted October 30, 2022
Abstract—The paper presents the results of paleomagnetic, rock magnetic, and cyclostratigraphic studies of
continental red beds that compose the Permian-Triassic boundary interval of the Staroe Slukino section in
the Vladimir Region, Russia. Based on the directions of the characteristic components of the natural rema-
nent magnetization of the studied rocks in the sampled stratum, the intervals of normal and reversed polarity
related to the regional magnetozones r RnP, r RnP, and N P-T were identified. Within the r RnP zone, there
2 3 3 3
is an interval of anomalous paleomagnetic directions, which has similar characteristics to those identified ear-
lier in the coeval intervals of the Nedubrovo, Zhukov Ravine, and Okskiy Siyezd sections. Revising the bio-
stratigraphy allows us to assume that the two zones of anomalous paleomagnetic directions in the composite
magnetic polarity scale of the upper Permian of the Russian Platform are a reflection of the same epoch of
an anomalous geomagnetic field configuration. It is estimated by the cyclostratigraphic method that the stud-
ied 16 m interval of the Staroe Slukino section took 900 ± 20 thousand years to accumulate, which limits the
duration of the geomagnetic field anomalous state near the Permian-Triassic boundary to ~110 thousand
years. A new Permian-Triassic (~252 Ma) paleomagnetic pole of the East European Platform is calculated:
plat = 36.3°; plong = 155.0°; dp/dm = 2.8°/4.8°.
Keywords: paleomagnetism, East European Platform, Russian Platform, Permian, Triassic, magnetostratig-
raphy, cyclostratigraphy, paleomagnetic pole
DOI: 10.1134/S1069351323020064

Fig. 1. The Staroe Slukino section: (a) stratigraphy, lithology, and sampling scheme; (b) location on the map of Eastern Europe;
(c) photograph of outcrop No. 1540(2167), beds 17–41, the Gorokhovets Member of the Obnora Formation, the Nefyodovian
and Zhukovian Regional Stages, upper Vyatkian Substage, the Upper Permian; (d) values of natural remanent magnetization
(NRM) and specific magnetic susceptibility; (e) latitude of the virtual geomagnetic pole (VGP). Legend: 1–15—sandstone; 2—
sandy siltstone; 3—siltstone; 4—argillaceous siltstone; 5—clay; 6—marl; 7—limestone; 8—talus; 9—red beds; 10—variegated
beds; 11—gray beds; 12—paleomagnetic sampling levels with a characteristic NRM component: normal polarity (a), reversed
polarity (b), with an anomalous magnetization component (c), with noisy paleomagnetic record (d); 13—normal (N) polarity
zones; 14—reversed (R) polarity zones; 15—zone of anomalous paleomagnetic directions.

IZVESTIYA, PHYSICS OF THE SOLID EARTH Vol. 59 No. 2 2023

### page_11
264 FETISOVA et al.
dom process that has some “memory”—each observa-
tion in it has a positive correlation with the previous
one. The power spectrum of such a process has an
increased density in the low frequency range, which is
reflected in the name of the noise by the word “red”.
These are the processes that describe many climatic
fluctuations on large time scales (Hasselman, 1976).
The periodograms contain the mean red noise spec-
trum and the confidence levels (CLs) corresponding
to various probabilities of difference from the null
hypothesis. For all the periodograms, the peaks above
90% (Fig. 7b) were combined into clusters by the K-
means method; the К value was determined by the
“elbow” method and is equal to 8 (Fig. 7c). The spec-
tral analysis was performed using Acycle v.2.4 software
(Li et al., 2019).
RESULTS AND DISCUSSION
The mean values of period lengths for the identified
clusters of peak frequencies in the periodograms are as
follows: (1) 187.8 cm; (2) 54.9 cm; (3) 35.4 cm;
(4)25.1 cm; (5) 17.5 cm; (6) 14.9 cm; (7) 12.5 cm; (8)
10.9 cm (Table 1). In this case, the clusters for fre-
quencies above 0.05 (clusters 4–8) cannot be clearly
distinguished: for different variants of the magnetic
susceptibility curves, the positions of the peaks differ
greatly, indicating that they are very prone to the mea-
surement positioning error in the section, so they were
excluded from consideration. The first four clusters
correspond to periods with length ratios of
1.00/3.43/5.31/7.48 (Table 1). According to the La04
model (Laskar et al., 2004), the duration of Milanko-
0.25 vitch cycles for an age of 250 Ma is 125.0 thousand
years; 95.0 thousand years (eccentricity), 36.3 thou-
sand years (tilt of the Earth’s rotation axis to the eclip-
0.20
tic), 22.0 thousand years; 20.9 thousand years;
17.9thousand years (precession), and the ratios of
0.15
their lengths are close to those for the periods that we
identified. Therefore, we can clearly correlate cluster 1
0.10 to cycles of eccentricity, cluster 2 to cycles of tilt of the
Earth’s rotation axis, and clusters 3 and 4 to cycles of
precession. This allows us to calculate that the sam-
0.05
pled interval of the section took 900 ± 20 thousand
years to accumulate.
